Drug note: the US bisoprolol label is for hypertension only and lists overt cardiac failure as a contraindication, so heart-failure use is off-label (guideline-supported: CIBIS-II, target 10 mg daily). name: Semaglutide (Wegovy)

regimen_warnings.text: Drug note: semaglutide titration is one labeled step at a time (0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 1.7, then 2.4 mg weekly), at least 4 weeks per step; escalation can be delayed 4 weeks for tolerability. 1.7 mg is a labeled maintenance dose, 2.4 mg is the dose studied in STEP-HFpEF (injection only; the oral tablets have no heart-failure data).

Drug note: Wegovy warnings: acute pancreatitis (not recommended to restart after pancreatitis; ask about history), gallbladder disease, and worsening of diabetic retinopathy (a larger absolute risk when retinopathy is present at baseline: 8.2% vs 5.2%).
Drug note: severe gastroparesis: GLP-1 receptor agonists slow gastric emptying and are not recommended in severe gastroparesis (Zepbound label; class caution).

Drug note: GI losses (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea) on a GLP-1 can cause volume depletion and acute kidney injury; with an SGLT2 inhibitor and a loop diuretic on board, counsel on fluids and consider reducing the diuretic if intake falls (Zepbound label; class caution).

This tool does not scale the effect by eGFR (no sourced multiplier): a dose that looks adequate on paper may under-diurese, so up-titrate to the observed weight response.

Number of days in a course is not set by the label (this tool prices 4 kits per course as an assumption).

monitoring_items.test: Loop diuretic response in advanced CKD
monitoring_items.timing: Daily weights and urine output; reassess within days of a dose change
monitoring_items.details: With eGFR below 30 less loop diuretic reaches the nephron, so higher doses are usually needed to reach the effective dose (torsemide and Furoscix labels; open-access reviews). This tool does not scale the effect by eGFR (no sourced multiplier): a dose that looks adequate on paper may under-diurese, so up-titrate to the observed weight response.

regimen_warnings.text: Drug note: Furoscix is a short course beside the oral loop diuretic, not a replacement; the label says "not for chronic use". Plan the return to the oral diuretic when congestion resolves. In significantly reduced renal function the fixed 80 mg dose may be insufficient and additional diuretic may be needed (Furoscix label).

checks: Less than 1 kg above dry weight (reserved for active congestion)
No oral loop diuretic on board (Furoscix is a short-course add-on to an oral loop, labeled "not for chronic use", not a replacement)
Anuria (label contraindication)
Documented furosemide / loop diuretic hypersensitivity
Documented adhesive / acrylate hypersensitivity

features.feature: Outpatient worsening-HF decongestion option on background loop therapy

name: Hydralazine/Isosorbide Dinitrate

regimen_warnings.text: Drug note: hydralazine can cause a drug-induced lupus-like syndrome (dose- and acetylator-dependent) and peripheral neuritis (pyridoxine / vitamin B6 is used for prevention or treatment) (BiDil label). Ask about joint pain, fever, rash and numbness or tingling at each visit.

Drug note: hydralazine can cause tachycardia and hypotension that may worsen ischemia (BiDil label; hypotension 8% vs 4% in A-HeFT). Titrate from one tablet three times daily to two tablets three times daily over several days as tolerated.

monitoring_items.details: Ask about arthralgia, fever, rash, pleuritic pain, numbness or tingling; check an ANA and CBC if symptoms appear; give pyridoxine if neuropathy develops (BiDil label).

checks: Concurrent PDE5 inhibitor (sildenafil / tadalafil / vardenafil / avanafil) — nitrate co-use risks profound, potentially fatal hypotension
Concurrent riociguat (soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator) — labeled contraindication with nitrates

features.feature: A-HeFT: mortality and HF-hospitalization benefit in self-identified Black patients, NYHA III-IV HFrEF, on a RAAS inhibitor and a beta-blocker (Class 1)

name: Ivabradine

facts.af_signal_note: Drug note: the Corlanor label reports more atrial fibrillation on ivabradine than on placebo. This patient has atrial fibrillation on record and is in sinus rhythm now; monitor the rhythm and stop if atrial fibrillation becomes persistent.

hr_continuation.basis: Corlanor label: reduce 2.5 mg bid if heart rate is below 50 or symptomatic, stop at 2.5 mg bid; increase only if heart rate is above 60

regimen_warnings.text: DDI WARNING: Ivabradine with verapamil or diltiazem (moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors and negative chronotropes): the Corlanor label says to avoid the combination (higher ivabradine exposure, additive heart-rate lowering).
DDI WARNING: Ivabradine with a CYP3A4 inducer (St John's wort, rifampin, barbiturates, phenytoin): the Corlanor label says to avoid it (lower ivabradine exposure, possible loss of effect).

checks: Pregnancy (may cause fetal harm)
Heart rate below 70 bpm: initiation requires HR 70 or higher (SHIFT)
Atrial fibrillation
Second-degree AV block
Third-degree AV block
Taking a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor (azole antifungals, clarithromycin, telithromycin, nelfinavir, ritonavir, nefazodone; labeled contraindication)

Liver disease, Child-Pugh B/C with severity not specified: ivabradine (label: Child-Pugh C) is contraindicated in severe hepatic impairment; if the patient is Child-Pugh B, select "Child-Pugh B confirmed (not C)" to allow it with caution
Sick sinus syndrome / sinoatrial block (labeled contraindication unless a demand pacemaker; a paced rhythm is excluded below)
Paced rhythm: pacemaker dependence cannot be excluded (labeled contraindication)
Acute decompensated heart failure (labeled contraindication; the tool reads NYHA IV, or NYHA III with congestion above dry weight, as acute decompensation)
Clinically significant hypotension (SBP below 90; labeled contraindication)

features.feature: SHIFT: Reduces HF hospitalization (sinus rhythm, LVEF <= 35; started at HR >= 70 on maximally tolerated beta-blocker; AHA/ACC 2022 Class 2a)

name: Vericiguat

source_differences.label: 5 mg once daily, or 2.5 mg if at risk of symptomatic hypotension (Verquvo label, revised January 2026)
source_differences.guideline: 2.5 mg once daily (2026 ESC Table 11; the VICTORIA starting dose)
source_differences.why: the label is the current dosing authority; 2.5 mg is used when systolic pressure is below 110 or chronic hypotension is recorded

regimen_warnings.text: Drug note: vericiguat label dosing: take with food; double about every 2 weeks as tolerated to the 10 mg target.
Drug note: vericiguat with riociguat or another soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator is contraindicated (Verquvo label).

Drug note: PDE-5 inhibitor (sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil, avanafil) with vericiguat: concomitant use is not recommended (Verquvo label; sildenafil added up to a 5.4 mmHg additional blood pressure drop). VICTORIA excluded PDE-5 inhibitors. Not a hard exclusion: weigh the indication and stop one agent where possible.

Drug note: long-acting nitrates (isosorbide dinitrate or mononitrate, including hydralazine/isosorbide dinitrate) were excluded from VICTORIA; the label does not prohibit the combination. Watch for additive hypotension and monitor blood pressure closely if both are used.

Drug note: NT-proBNP above 8,000 pg/mL: in VICTORIA no benefit was seen in the highest NT-proBNP group (about 14% of the cohort, 672 of 4,805; primary outcome HR 1.16, 95% CI 0.94-1.41; at or below 8,000 HR 0.85). The label has no upper limit; this is an advisory, not an exclusion.

Drug note: systolic pressure below 100 mmHg: VICTORIA excluded SBP below 100 or symptomatic hypotension (a trial criterion; the label has no SBP threshold). Start at 2.5 mg, titrate only if blood pressure is tolerated, and recheck blood pressure after each step.

Drug note: eGFR below 15 mL/min or dialysis: vericiguat was studied only with eGFR 15 or higher (Verquvo label; VICTORIA excluded eGFR below 15). No data support use here; this is a caution, not a label contraindication.

checks: Pregnancy (FDA boxed warning, embryo-fetal toxicity)
Concurrent riociguat or another soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator — labeled contraindication
NYHA class not II-IV — initiation criterion (VICTORIA)
LVEF 45 or higher — initiation criterion (VICTORIA)
NT-proBNP missing or below the VICTORIA threshold (1000 pg/mL in sinus rhythm, 1600 pg/mL in atrial fibrillation or other rhythms) — initiation criterion
No qualifying worsening-HF event (HF hospitalization within 6 months, or outpatient IV diuretic within 3 months) — initiation criterion (VICTORIA)

regimen_warnings.text: Drug note: take other oral medicines at least 3 hours before or after patiromer (it can bind them and reduce absorption).
Drug note: avoid patiromer in severe constipation, bowel obstruction or impaction; it can slow bowel motility.

monitoring_items.details: Hypomagnesemia occurred in 5.3% in the label trials (about 9% had Mg below 1.4 mg/dL). Check magnesium and replace if low.

regimen_warnings.text: Drug note (heart failure): Lokelma carries about 400 mg of sodium per 5 g (800 mg per 10 g) and causes dose-related edema (4.4% at 5 g, 5.9% at 10 g, 16.1% at 15 g; placebo 2.4%). Watch weight and edema, limit dietary sodium, and be ready to increase the diuretic.
Drug note: take other oral medicines at least 2 hours before or after Lokelma (its effect on gastric pH changes absorption of some drugs, e.g. furosemide, atorvastatin, dabigatran, tacrolimus).
Drug note: avoid Lokelma in severe constipation, bowel obstruction or impaction, or abnormal post-operative bowel motility (not studied).

Drug note (2026 ESC heart failure guideline): REALIZE-K showed a signal of more heart failure deterioration with sodium zirconium cyclosilicate and the trial was not powered for outcomes; the guideline makes no recommendation for potassium binders. Use it to enable guideline therapy only with the sodium and edema monitoring above.

monitoring_items.details: Lokelma sodium load can cause fluid retention. Check weight, edema and diuretic need after starting or raising the dose.

features.feature: Sodium load risk in congested HF (about 400 mg sodium per 5 g; dose-related edema)

name: Ferric Carboxymaltose

regimen_warnings.text: Drug note (2026 ESC heart failure guideline): a transferrin saturation (TSAT) below 20% identifies the patients most likely to benefit from IV iron; the engine criteria (ferritin below 100, or 100-300 with TSAT below 20%) are unchanged.

Drug note: BOXED WARNING (Injectafer label, 08/2026): symptomatic, severe and prolonged hypophosphatemia, including osteomalacia and fractures, has occurred, also in patients with a normal baseline phosphate. Correct pre-existing hypophosphatemia first; check serum phosphate before any repeat course within 3 months and in patients at risk (malabsorption, inflammatory bowel disease, vitamin D deficiency, hyperparathyroidism).

monitoring_items.timing: Before any repeat course within 3 months, and when symptoms of bone pain or weakness occur
monitoring_items.details: Hypophosphatemia can be severe and prolonged and cause osteomalacia and fractures, even with a normal baseline. Check phosphate before repeat dosing, especially with malabsorption, IBD, vitamin D deficiency or hyperparathyroidism (Injectafer label).
Maintenance 500 mg is given only if ferritin is below 100 ng/mL, or 100-300 ng/mL with TSAT below 20% (Injectafer label). No data beyond 36 weeks.

checks: Hemoglobin 15 g/dL or higher — no label data (hold ferric carboxymaltose)

features.feature: Treats iron deficiency in HFrEF (LVEF 40 or lower; Class 2a)
Treats iron deficiency, limited evidence at LVEF 41-49 (trials enrolled LVEF below 50)

name: Digoxin

monitoring_items.timing: After starting or changing the dose, after any renal change or interacting drug, and when toxicity is suspected (no interval is stated in the sections read)
monitoring_items.details: 2026 ESC heart failure guideline: target serum concentration below 1.2 ng/mL (the guideline gives the target; the plasma level guides dosing). Check potassium, magnesium and kidney function with it.

regimen_warnings.text: DIGOXIN SAFETY: Wolff-Parkinson-White / accessory pathway (Lanoxin label warning 5.1): in atrial fibrillation with an accessory pathway digoxin can accelerate conduction over the pathway and cause ventricular fibrillation. Avoid unless the pathway has been treated or a specialist directs it.

DIGOXIN SAFETY: Potassium above 5.5 mEq/L. The label has no potassium contraindication (hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia and hypercalcemia are the toxicity predisposers); correct the hyperkalemia, check an ECG, and recheck the digoxin level before relying on this regimen.

DIGOXIN SAFETY: eGFR below 15. The label has no renal contraindication; dosing follows its table by lean body weight and creatinine clearance (the 62.5 mcg tier is the lowest offered). Expect accumulation: check a level in 5-7 days and after any renal change.

checks: Ventricular fibrillation (labeled contraindication)
Renal function not entered (digoxin is renally cleared; obtain a BMP before starting)
Potassium below 3.5 mEq/L
Second-degree AV block
Third-degree AV block

name: Metolazone

hypokalemia_caution_below_k.basis: engine policy; the label warns of rapid severe hypokalemia, dose-related, and has no potassium contraindication

monitoring_items.test: Basic metabolic panel (sodium, potassium) after starting metolazone
monitoring_items.timing: Within about 3-5 days of starting, then at regular intervals (the day count is practice-based, not label text)
monitoring_items.details: Label: rapid-onset severe hyponatremia and/or hypokalemia can occur, rarely even after the initial doses, and hyponatremia can occur at any time during long-term therapy; check potassium at regular intervals. Hypokalemia is dose-related and is a hazard with digoxin; adding it to a loop diuretic can cause large fluid and electrolyte losses.

facts.chronic_use_review: Thiazide-type diuretics are for short-term use in diuretic resistance (2026 ESC); chronic use in a stable, euvolemic patient should be avoided. Review whether it is still needed, with sodium, potassium and kidney function checked. This is a prompt to review, not an instruction to stop.

regimen_warnings.text: Drug note (2026 ESC heart failure guideline): a thiazide-type diuretic is added for persistent congestion on a loop diuretic (diuretic resistance, or eGFR below 30 with close monitoring); it is short-term. Recheck electrolytes and kidney function within days and stop once decongested.

Drug note: metolazone can cause severe hyponatremia and hypokalemia, sometimes within the first doses, especially added to a loop diuretic. Check sodium and potassium soon after starting and at regular intervals (Zaroxolyn label).

checks: eGFR below 15 (anuria/ESRD; no tubular function for the thiazide mechanism)
Anuria (label contraindication)
